property_summary: After any successful external Put call by any sender with any nonzero value, the contract remains unlocked so a subsequent Put by the same sender (or any sender) still succeeds; the mutant that never resets locked_ will permanently lock after the first Put and cause later Put calls to revert.

For any sender and any nonzero payable amount, after performing a successful Put call the contract remains non-locked so a subsequent Put by the same sender with another payable amount also succeeds; the mutant that never resets locked_ will permanently lock after the first Put and make a later Put revert.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, two sequential successful Put calls (from possibly different callers) must both succeed on the reference; the mutant that never resets the reentrancy lock causes the second Put to revert after the first succeeds.

For any externally owned caller A and nonzero ether value v (admissible domain), performing two sequential Put calls from A with value v should both succeed on the correct contract (the reentrancy lock is cleared after each call), whereas the mutant that never resets locked_ will make the second Put revert (permanently locked after first call).

For any caller and any payable amount >= MinSum, the reference contract allows a Put call to succeed (returns/does not revert) even if a previously executed Put triggered a call into an external contract that reverts; the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock can become permanently locked by such a failing callback and make a subsequent Put revert.

For any caller and any Ether value, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored acc.unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp in the reference (it is floored to block.timestamp), but the mutant allows acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs (caller-supplied _unlockTime in the past).

For every call to Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least block.timestamp (floored), whereas the mutant allows storing unlockTime < block.timestamp when caller supplies a past timestamp.

After any Put(...) call by any actor with any value, the correct contract always stores Acc[actor].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it floors to now); the mutant can store Acc[actor].unlockTime < block.timestamp when given a past _unlockTime, so there exist fuzzed inputs (actor and _unlockTime) that make the mutant violate this.

For any caller and any payable amount, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract guarantees that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it floors to now); the mutant that unconditionally writes _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime (a past timestamp), violating this invariant.

For any caller and any payable amount, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the correct contract always stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it floors to now); the mutant that blindly writes _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any sent value, after calling Put(...) with that value the contract's recorded balance for the caller increases by at least the sent value (i.e. Acc[msg].balance >= msg.value after the call); the mutant that removes updating acc.balance can violate this (recorded balance does not reflect the deposit).

After a caller invokes Put with a positive msg.value, the contract's stored Acc[caller].balance is at least msg.value (i.e., the deposit is recorded); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance can leave Acc[caller].balance == 0 for some positive deposit, violating this rule.

For any caller and any positive deposit value, calling Put records the deposit by increasing Acc[caller].balance by exactly the deposited amount (i.e., Acc[caller].balance after Put equals its previous balance plus msg.value); the mutant that omits updating acc.balance can leave Acc[caller].balance unchanged, violating this.

For any caller and any deposit value, calling Put preserves that the contract's ETH balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value and the call succeeds; the mutant still increases contract ETH (because payable), but the stored Acc[msg.sender].balance may not reflect deposits — instead we assert that address(c).balance increases by msg.value (which the mutant still satisfies) so to distinguish we instead rely on the public getter Acc to show that when transfer is made via fallback through a contract that forwards value but has code, the correct contract records the deposit whereas the mutant does not; specifically: when a caller that is a contract with payable fallback forwards a deposit via c.Put, the reference increments Acc[caller].balance while the mutant leaves it unchanged, so requiring Acc[caller].balance >= msg.value after Put is the invariant the reference satisfies and the mutant can violate it for some inputs.

For any caller-contract and any deposit amount, if a contract caller invokes Put(value) on C, then C.Acc[caller].balance increases by at least the deposited value (the good contract records deposits coming from contract callers); the mutant that removed updating acc.balance can be called by a contract that forwards value and have Acc[caller].balance unchanged, violating this.
After a successful Collect call that transfers _am, the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance decreases by exactly _am only if the external transfer succeeded.

property_summary: Calling Collect with valid parameters should not revert when the caller has enough recorded balance and the unlock time has passed.
If Collect is called with amount at least MinSum and caller had enough recorded balance and unlockTime passed, then the call must not revert.
If the caller's recorded balance is at least MinSum and at least the requested amount and unlockTime has passed, then Collect should not revert (i.e., succeed).
If the caller's recorded balance is >= MinSum and >= requested amount and unlockTime passed, then Collect must not revert when invoked by that same externally owned account.

Invariant: After a successful Collect call that attempts to send funds, the contract's recorded holder balance is decreased by the withdrawn amount; the mutant removes the check of the external call result and therefore can decrement balance even when the external transfer fails (e.g., callee reverts), violating the invariant.

For every Collect(amount) call that targets a callee which reverts on receiving ether, the correct contract C preserves the holder's balance (because it only deducts after a successful external call), whereas the mutant deducts the balance even when the external call fails, breaking the invariant.

For any caller, if Collect(amount) is invoked when the holder has >= MinSum and >= amount and unlockTime passed, then after Collect returns the holder's recorded balance is decreased by amount iff the external ether transfer to the caller actually succeeded; the mutant always decreases the balance even when the external call fails.

For any caller and amount where Collect is allowed (balance>=MinSum, balance>=amount, unlockTime passed), the reference contract only deducts the holder balance when the external transfer to the caller succeeds; the mutant always deducts the balance even if the external transfer fails, so there exist inputs (a failing callee and amount) where the mutant decreases the stored balance while the reference does not.

For any holder and amount that meet Collect's preconditions, calling Collect either (A) succeeds in sending ether to the caller and then decreases the stored balance by the amount, or (B) the external transfer fails and the reference contract preserves the stored balance; the mutant can decrease the stored balance even when the external transfer fails, so there exist inputs (a failing recipient and an amount) where reference preserves balance but mutant does not.
After a successful Collect that sends funds, the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance is strictly decreased by the collected amount.

If Collect(...) reverts then the call reverted when the requested amount exceeds the contract's recorded balance for that caller or caller had insufficient unlocked balance — Collect must not revert for valid requests under the original ordering.

If a caller requests to Collect an amount <= their recorded balance and after the call the external transfer reverted, then the original contract must not revert (i.e., Collect should succeed) whereas the mutant can revert when external send fails.

If Collect is called for an account that meets MinSum and unlockTime and the external transfer would fail, the original contract returns success (doesn't revert) while the mutant may revert; therefore for such valid calls the original never reverts.
For callers whose recorded balance meets MinSum and is at least the requested amount and whose unlockTime is in the past, Collect never reverts (original succeeds but mutant may revert).
